q: Did games with smaller crowds coincide with smaller national TV audiences in 2025 and 2026?
report:
Yes on the raw numbers: comparing games on the same network, smaller crowds went with smaller national TV audiences (correlation 0.34 in 2025, n = 82, range 0.14 to 0.52; 0.47 in 2026, n = 83, range 0.29 to 0.62)[1]. Mostly no after comparing each game with its own park's usual crowd, so popular teams do not drive the result: the correlation falls to 0.16 in 2025 (range -0.05 to 0.37) and 0.14 in 2026 (range -0.08 to 0.34), and both ranges include zero[2]. Across team-seasons, teams with bigger average crowds also had bigger average national TV audiences (correlation 0.52, n = 56, range 0.30 to 0.69), which is consistent with team-level factors such as popularity and market size driving both, though the data does not prove the cause[3].

*Viewership figures are publicly reported and may differ from official Nielsen data. They are the national TV audience, excluding streaming add-ons. Nielsen changed its method on September 1, 2025, so 2025 and 2026 figures are not like-for-like. These are associations, not cause and effect.*

q: Do Cubs Sunday games draw better than their Tuesday games?
report: Yes, Chicago Cubs Sunday home games consistently draw larger crowds than their Tuesday home games[1]. Overall from 2024 to 2026, Sunday attendance was higher than Tuesday attendance by an average of 1,860 fans, with Sundays averaging 37,140 (89.9% fill rate) and Tuesdays averaging 35,280 (85.4% fill rate), representing a gap of 4.5 percentage points[1]. In 2024, Sunday attendance was higher by 2,549 fans, with Sundays averaging 36,916 (89.4% fill rate) and Tuesdays averaging 34,367 (83.2% fill rate), a gap of 6.2 percentage points[2]. For the 2025 season, Sundays were higher by 1,459 fans, averaging 37,262 (90.2% fill rate) compared to Tuesdays at 35,802 (86.7% fill rate), a gap of 3.5 percentage points[2]. Finally, in 2026, Sunday attendance was higher by 1,658 fans, averaging 37,260 (90.2% fill rate) compared to Tuesdays at 35,602 (86.2% fill rate), a gap of 4.0 percentage points[2].

q: What drives MLB attendance?

chart.title: Change in attendance by factor
labels: Games against the Los Angeles Dodgers, compared with the average opponent

report:
Major League Baseball attendance increases coincide with home openers, matchups against high-profile opponents, Saturday games, and strong team performance[1]. Specifically, home openers coincide with a 69.1% increase in game attendance[1]. Playing against the Los Angeles Dodgers coincides with a 25.0% attendance increase compared with the average opponent, while playing the New York Yankees coincides with a 15.7% increase, the Chicago Cubs with a 13.1% increase, and the Philadelphia Phillies with a 9.5% increase[1]. Saturday games coincide with an 8.8% increase compared with Friday games[1]. In contrast, weekday games coincide with lower attendance compared with Fridays, as Mondays coincide with a 21.8% decrease, Wednesdays with a 20.6% decrease, and Tuesdays with an 18.9% decrease[1]. For overall team factors, a season win rate .100 higher coincides with an 8.6% increase in attendance, and having a 10% higher crowd over the prior two years coincides with an 8.2% increase[1].

*These are associations, not cause and effect.*
